lead: A deterministic finite automaton (DFA) is a machine with finite memory. It reads an input string one symbol at a time. Its whole memory is one state, chosen from a finite set. The state stores only what the past has done that can change the future. A DFA is used to check patterns: does a login name end in 01, is the number of a's divisible by 3, does a protocol frame contain the flag 01. It is the simplest full model of a computer with no extra storage.
prereq: You need 1.1: alphabets, strings, languages, Σ*, and the empty string ε.

sections.h3: The five parts of a DFA

blocks.text: A DFA is a 5-tuple M = (Q, Σ, δ, q<sub>0</sub>, F). Each part has one job. The tuple is the machine. The diagram is only a picture of the tuple.

blocks.where: Q is the finite non-empty set of states; Σ is the input alphabet; δ is the transition function; q<sub>0</sub> is the start state; F is the set of final states.

items: Q: finite and non-empty. Each state is one possible value of the machine's memory.
Σ: a finite set of input symbols. The input string is a word in Σ*.
δ: Q × Σ → Q. Read δ(p, a) = q as: from state p on symbol a, go to state q.
q<sub>0</sub> ∈ Q: the state before any symbol is read.
F ⊆ Q: the final or accepting states. A run that ends in F accepts.

blocks.text: For example, Q = {A, B, C}, Σ = {0, 1}, q<sub>0</sub> = A, F = {C} is a DFA once δ is given for all six pairs. A table with one row per state and one column per symbol can list δ. A diagram with circles and labelled arrows is shorthand for the same tuple. Some syllabi call the diagram itself the simplified notation; it is not a separate definition.
Determinism means exactly one next state for each state and each symbol. δ is a function, not a relation. There is no choice and no ε-move. A DFA cannot change state without reading a symbol from Σ.

A run on w = a<sub>1</sub>a<sub>2</sub>…a<sub>n</sub> is the state sequence r<sub>0</sub>, r<sub>1</sub>, …, r<sub>n</sub>. Here r<sub>0</sub> = q<sub>0</sub> and r<sub>i</sub> = δ(r<sub>i−1</sub>, a<sub>i</sub>) for i = 1 to n. Each a<sub>i</sub> is one input symbol.
L(M) = { w ∈ Σ* : the run on w ends in a state of F }
blocks.where: L(M) is the language accepted by M; w is an input string; F is the set of final states.

blocks.text: The empty string ε is accepted exactly when q0 ∈ F. Acceptance depends only on the final state of the run. Earlier states do not matter. The extended transition function δ̂, which gives the final state directly, is in 1.3.

A dead state, also called a trap state, is a non-final state that loops to itself on every symbol. Add a dead state whenever a transition is missing. A table with a blank cell is not a DFA, because δ must be total.
To design a DFA, list the questions about the past that change the future. Each answer is a state. Store nothing else. This one rule covers most exam designs.
Strings ending in ab over Σ = {a, b}: remember whether the last symbol was a. Use states for no a yet or last symbol not a, last symbol a, and the final state for the suffix ab.
Strings containing 01 over Σ = {0, 1}: use states for no 0 seen, a 0 seen but no 01 yet, and found 01. The found state is final and loops to itself on 0 and 1.
Number of a's divisible by 3 over Σ = {a, b}: use states 0, 1, 2 for the count modulo 3. On a, move i to (i + 1) mod 3. On b, stay at i. State 0 is both start and final.

Strings with no two consecutive 1s: use states for no 1 yet or last symbol 0, last symbol 1, and a dead state after 11. From the last-symbol-1 state, a 1 goes to the dead state. The first state (no 1 yet, or last symbol 0) is start and final; the last-symbol-1 state is final; the dead state after 11 is not final.
The worked example below applies this method to strings ending in 01. The figure shows the finished machine.

figure.caption: Each state remembers the longest suffix that could still become 01: A for none, B for 0, C for 01, the only accepting state. 1001 ends in C and is accepted; 110 ends in B and is rejected. From C, a 1 goes back to A.

spec.aria: A three-state DFA: A loops on 1 and goes to B on 0; B loops on 0 and goes to C on 1; C, double-circled, goes to B on 0 and back to A on 1, with the runs of 1001 and 110 below.

examples.question: Design a DFA over Σ = {0, 1} that accepts exactly the strings ending in 01. Test it on 1001 and 110.
steps: The future depends on the longest suffix of the input that is also a prefix of the target 01. The prefixes are ε, 0, 01.
Name the states by that suffix: A = ε (start), B = 0, C = 01 (final). So Q = {A, B, C}, q<sub>0</sub> = A, F = {C}.
Fill each transition by appending the symbol and keeping the longest suffix that is a prefix of 01.
A on 1: suffix 1, longest prefix ε, so go to A. A on 0: suffix 0, so go to B.
B on 0: suffix 00, longest prefix 0, so go to B. B on 1: suffix 01, so go to C.
C on 0: suffix 010, longest prefix 0, so go to B. C on 1: suffix 011, longest prefix ε, so go to A.
Read 1001: A, A, B, B, C. The run ends in C, and C ∈ F, so 1001 is accepted.
Read 110: A, A, A, B. The run ends in B, and B ∉ F, so 110 is rejected.
examples.answer: The DFA has Q = {A, B, C}, q<sub>0</sub> = A, F = {C}, and the six transitions above; it accepts 1001 and rejects 110.

traps: A table with missing entries is not a DFA. δ must be total, so add a dead state rather than leaving a cell blank.
The start state may itself be final. Then ε is accepted, even though no symbol has been read.
A final state still needs all its outgoing moves. Final means accepting, not stopping.
Ends in 01 is not the same as contains 01. For ends in, C on 1 goes back to A. For contains, the final state loops on both 0 and 1.
ε is not an input symbol of a DFA. Only symbols from Σ appear on arrows.

quiz.q: Define a DFA as a 5-tuple and state the meaning of each part.
quiz.a: M = (Q, Σ, δ, q<sub>0</sub>, F). Q is a finite non-empty set of states; Σ is the input alphabet; δ: Q × Σ → Q is the total transition function; q<sub>0</sub> ∈ Q is the start state; F ⊆ Q is the set of final states.

quiz.q: Why must δ be total? What goes wrong with a blank cell in the transition table?
quiz.a: A DFA must have exactly one next state for every state and symbol. A blank cell gives no move, so the run can stop before the input ends. The object is then not a DFA under the formal definition. Add a dead state to fill the cell.

quiz.q: Use the DFA of the worked example. Give the state sequence for 0101 and say whether it is accepted.
quiz.a: Start A. 0 sends A to B, 1 sends B to C, 0 sends C to B, 1 sends B to C. The sequence is A, B, C, B, C. It ends in C ∈ F, so 0101 is accepted.

quiz.q: Design a DFA over Σ = {a, b} for strings in which the number of a's is divisible by 3. List the states and transitions.
quiz.a: States 0, 1, 2 for count mod 3. Start state 0, final state 0. On a: 0→1, 1→2, 2→0. On b: each state stays at itself. This accepts ε (0 a's), aaa (3 a's), and abaa (3 a's). It rejects a, aa, aba and ab.

quiz.q: A machine has a transition table with one blank cell and no dead state. Is it a DFA under the formal definition? Explain.
quiz.a: No. δ must be a total function from Q × Σ to Q. A blank cell means δ is undefined for that state-symbol pair. The run on some strings would have no next state, so the formal definition fails.

quiz.q: Why can a DFA not count an arbitrary number of a's and then compare with another count?
quiz.a: A DFA has only finitely many states. Each state can store only a fixed amount of information, such as a count modulo a fixed number. An arbitrary count needs unbounded memory, so no finite state set can hold it. Extra memory needs a pushdown automaton or a Turing machine.

quiz.q: What is a trap state, and when do you add one?
quiz.a: A trap state is a non-final state that loops to itself on every input symbol. Add one when a transition would otherwise be missing, so that δ becomes total.

beyond: Not for the exam. DFAs sit inside lexical analyzers, regular-expression search, and simple protocol checkers. Hardware controllers use the same one-state-per-symbol-step idea. Many tools compile regular expressions into DFAs for fast matching. Search next for DFA minimization and the subset construction, or for regular expression to DFA.
